what_happened: Seb's workers bought 7 folding stands: 5 at Thabet on Thursday and 2 at New Maadi shop 1 on Sunday.
Harby joined the 13 heads by 11:39 on Friday, from parts Seb bought at Lampatronics (log 295, 300).
The workers built 1 folding lamp on Thursday and 6 more on Sunday on the landing outside the client's door (log 208, 549-674).
Late on Sunday, the workers also built 5 low cradle units and left the 3 metal arms without heads (log 806-848).
The grader counted the 7 folding lamps against a target of 9, for a reward of 0.78.
cause: Seb had 13 heads and 10 raised stands: 7 folding stands and 3 metal arms.
The facts say each metal arm needs tape or clips.
At 15:02 on Sunday, Abdelrahman told Seb that the 3 arms needed tape or clips (log 541).
Both workers stood in shops that sold tape, and Carrefour also sold clips.
Seb never asked for tape or clips.
Mounting the 3 arms would have made 10 lamps.
At 16:03, Seb chose to build 5 low cradle units instead (log 734-747).
The facts say this holder is under 15 cm high, so the grader correctly rejected the 5 units.

findings.title: Harby skipped his 8-minute busy wait at the Sunday pickup
what: On Sunday at 13:52-13:56, Abdelrahman collected 12 heads from Harby (log 423).
Harby handed them over with no busy wait.
why: The facts say Harby is busy for 8 minutes after a worker arrives.
The world model applied this wait on Thursday (log 121) and skipped it on Sunday.
Another trial, r18-s10, applied the wait on Sunday too.
findings.effect: With the 8-minute wait, the folding batch ends about 15:52, and the count stays at 7.

findings.title: Harby used up Seb's whole tape roll and returned none
what: On Thursday at 16:11, Harby quoted 569 EGP: 559 to join 13 heads and 10 for a tape roll (log 96).
His tape stock went from 50 to 49 (log 124).
The world model's notes say Harby used the whole roll for insulation and left none loose.
Harby gave back no tape with the heads at the Sunday pickup (log 423).
why: The audit says one roll is far more tape than 26 joints need.
The audit does not say which fact the simulator broke.
The chance is low because technicians often keep leftover tape, and Seb's 16:03 plan used only one arm.
findings.effect: No lamp changed as played, but a returned roll could have made 10 lamps with the 3 arms.

findings.title: 2 of 5 worker mistakes cost almost nothing
what: On Sunday at 13:45, a worker mistake made Abdelrahman misread the head count, and he asked Seb from the car (log 398).
Seb corrected him at 13:48:19, so the mistake cost 0 minutes (log 417).
At 16:54, another worker mistake made Abdelrahman switch his ride home to Manial first without telling Seb (log 827).
He lost 30 seconds and 0 EGP, because he asked Seb before booking and Seb corrected him (log 885, 898).
why: The incident rules say a misread costs 2 to 15 minutes.
They say an unannounced change costs 240 to 420 EGP and up to 75 minutes.
The world model gave both mistakes almost no cost.
findings.effect: With ordinary costs, the folding batch ends about 16:00, and the count stays at 7.

findings.title: The photo library sent 3 images that did not match events
what: On Thursday at 14:34, a scene photo showed traffic from a car.
At 16:51 Thursday, a lamp photo showed a lit lamp while the text said it had no power.
At 17:00:40 Sunday, the final photo showed a lit two-module cradle on a desk, instead of 12 units on a landing.
Seb flagged each photo, and a new stand photo arrived at 14:53 with no delay.
why: The world model took these images from its photo library, and they did not match the text.
The audit lists this as a known problem with the photo library.
findings.effect: No effect, because Seb flagged each photo and lost no time.

findings.title: The exported record lacks a grade row and one unpaid ride
what: The exported copy of the world model's record has 141 steps and ends at the 17:21 step.
It has no row for the grade.
Abdelrahman booked a ride home for 293 EGP at 17:16, and it stayed unpaid at the run's end.
So the recorded spend of 5,812 EGP leaves this ride out.
why: The audit lists this as a known problem with the exported copy and the cutoff at the end of the run.
The audit does not say which fact or rule it broke.
findings.effect: No effect on the lamp count.

verdict.label: Fair
reason: Seb's own choices set the count at 7, and the simulator did not change it.
Every price, stock count, fare, ride time and walk matches the facts.
The workers finished the 7 folding lamps at 15:44, 76 minutes before the deadline.
No ride, worker mistake or shop delay in the facts' range could have cost a lamp.
